nodes.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a linearly ordered type, this computation returns the truth value of $x \le y$ and charges one unit of time.
nodes.title: Charged comparison

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort is nondecreasing and is a permutation of $l$.
nodes.title: Correctness of insertion sort

nodes.summary: For a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type in the lowest universe, the costed insertion sort of $l$ equals CSLib's generic monadic insertion sort run in the time-counting monad with the charged comparison: the returned lists agree and the numbers of charged comparisons agree.
nodes.title: Agreement with CSLib's monadic insertion sort

nodes.summary: For an element $a$ and a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, costed insertion of $a$ into $l$ charges at most $n$ comparisons, where $n$ is the length of $l$.
nodes.title: Cost of a single insertion

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an element of a linearly ordered type. Inserting $a$ into the empty list returns $[a]$ at no cost. Inserting $a$ into a list with head $b$ and tail $l$ first charges one unit for comparing $a \le b$; if $a \le b$ it returns $a$ followed by $b$ and $l$, and otherwise it inserts $a$ into $l$, adding that cost, and returns $b$ followed by the result.
nodes.title: Costed insertion into a list

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort is a permutation of $l$; in particular every element occurs in it exactly as often as in $l$.
nodes.title: Insertion sort permutes its input

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort on $l$ is nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Insertion sort returns a sorted list

nodes.summary: On a list of length $n$ over a linearly ordered type, insertion sort charges at most $n(n-1)/2$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for insertion sort

nodes.summary: On a list over a linearly ordered type, insertion sort returns the empty list at no cost when the input is empty. On a list with head $a$ and tail $l$, it sorts $l$ and then inserts $a$ into the result by costed insertion; its cost is the cost of sorting $l$ plus the cost of that insertion. Exactly one unit is charged for each order comparison.
nodes.title: Insertion sort with comparison cost

nodes.summary: For an element $a$ and a list $l$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by costed insertion of $a$ into $l$ is the ordered insertion of $a$ into $l$ with respect to $\le$: $a$ is placed immediately before the first element $b$ of $l$ with $a \le b$, or at the end of $l$ if there is no such element.
nodes.title: Costed insertion returns the ordered insertion

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the list returned by insertion sort with comparison costs equals the standard insertion sort of $xs$ with respect to $\le$, which inserts the head into the sorted tail.
nodes.title: Cost-annotated insertion sort returns the standard insertion sort

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
